author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty page lists every specialty the clinic records by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it shown by full name, all on one page. It is reached by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: GET /specialties.html renders a page listing every specialty the clinic records, each by its stored name, all on a single page with no paging.
Under each specialty, every veterinarian holding it is listed by full name, first name then last name (seed example: Helen Leary under radiology).
A veterinarian holding more than one specialty is listed under each of them (seed example: Linda Douglas under both surgery and dentistry).
A veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page (seed examples: James Carter, Sharon Jenkins).
A specialty held by no veterinarian is still listed, with no veterinarian under it (PRD edge case 3).
Specialties, and the veterinarians under each, appear in the same stable order on every opening (PRD edge case 4).
With no specialty recorded, the page still opens and lists none (PRD edge case 5).

Specialty names appear exactly as stored whichever supported language the page is presented in (PRD edge case 6); any wording the page itself adds is present in every supported language per REQ-LANG-002, and the page carries the standard navigation per REQ-SYS-001.
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application: NG-2 is unchanged (owner decision, intake line 1: 'managing veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before').

A navigation entry, or a link from any other page, to the specialty page (owner decision, intake line 1: 'no navigation entry and no link from another page is part of this request'). Deferred to a possible follow-up; recorded as a PRD Open Question.
Paging the specialty list (owner request: 'All specialties render on one page — no pagination').
Listing the full veterinarian roster on the specialty page (owner request: 'the page lists specialties, not the full vet roster').
Filtering or searching veterinarians by specialty: the page is a complete listing with no query input, and NG-9 stands unchanged.
Translating specialty names: they appear by their stored name (owner request).
A machine-readable form of the specialty list: the owner asked for a page only.
Any change to the veterinarian directory's behavior under REQ-VET-001.
notes: Boundary check: no contradiction with a recorded requirement or Non-Goals row. NG-2 is untouched because the page is read-only. NG-9 is untouched because the page lists every specialty and takes no search input. REQ-SYS-001 still binds the page's own navigation, and the owner's decision excludes only inbound links. No Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides. No ubiquitous-language terms were resolved at intake, so the vocabulary file is unchanged. Open questions resolved to the narrowest reading, per the owner's instruction, and recorded in PRD Open Questions: (1) a specialty with no holder is listed with nothing under it, with no 'none' label; (2) order is committed only as stable, with no particular order named; (3) the visible entry point is deferred. Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records exist, so it was skipped. PRD delta: Context sentence, provenance-banner exception for REQ-VET-003, narrative plus 4 Done-when bullets, edge cases 3-6, and 3 Open Questions.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the vet package with in-force catalog patterns only (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog: Repository, Web controller, Value object); no new package, no cross-package dependency, no entity or schema change. Small adjustment recorded in docs/system-design.md: three Contracts rows (SpecialtyRepository, SpecialtyDirectory, SpecialtyController), REQ-VET-003 joined to Vet/Specialty/VetRepository rows, a Specialty directory invariants paragraph, the vet/ package line, and a provenance-banner exception for the REQ-VET-003 statements. Shape: package-private SpecialtyController maps GET /specialties.html, reads every specialty from a new SpecialtyRepository and every vet from the existing cached VetRepository.findAll(), hands both to SpecialtyDirectory, and renders vets/specialtyList. SpecialtyDirectory is an immutable value object built by a pure static factory from (specialties, vets): it inverts each Vet's own specialty set, keeps holderless specialties, omits vets with no specialty, and fixes a total order itself. Covering code resolved by grep (weaker basis, IDE oracle not connected): VetRepository.java findAll() @Cacheable("vets") with no ORDER BY; PetTypeRepository.java lookup-repository precedent; BaseEntity.java defines no equals/hashCode; layout.html menuItem highlights by active==menu.
integration_points: Entry point GET /specialties.html -> SpecialtyController -> SpecialtyRepository (all specialties) + VetRepository.findAll() (existing cached read, unchanged) -> SpecialtyDirectory factory -> model attribute -> view vets/specialtyList.

Binding target: none. The handler binds no request input (no @RequestParam, @PathVariable, or @ModelAttribute) and binds no persisted type; no @InitBinder is needed. The lang parameter is consumed by the system package's locale interceptor (WebConfiguration), not by the handler.
Double, SpecialtyDirectory unit tests: no boundary crossed; real Vet and Specialty instances built in the test (testing-principles § Mocking Policy: never mock domain objects).
Double, framework transport in SpecialtyControllerTests: MockMvc via @WebMvcTest(SpecialtyController.class), the sanctioned transport stand-in (testing-principles § Mocking Policy).

Double, repository boundary in SpecialtyControllerTests: hand-written in-memory implementations of SpecialtyRepository and VetRepository registered as beans through a @TestConfiguration imported into the web test; not @MockitoBean (testing-principles § Mocking Policy: hand-write first, framework stubs a conscious exception). SpecialtyRepository extends the narrow Repository<Specialty, Integer> base, as VetRepository does, so the double stays hand-writable; the VetRepository double answers findAll() from fixtures and may throw UnsupportedOperationException from the paged method this surface never calls.

View: vets/specialtyList uses the fragments/layout fragment for the standard navigation (REQ-SYS-001) with an active-menu value matching no menu item, and adds no menu item (prd-entry non-goal: no navigation entry).

Test placement per testing-principles § Test Pyramid: inversion, omission, holderless specialty, and ordering rules live in SpecialtyDirectory and are tested there (theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListAVetUnderEverySpecialtyTheyHold, ...OmitVetsHoldingNoSpecialty, ...ListASpecialtyHeldByNoVet, ...ListSpecialtiesAndHoldersInAStableOrder); rendering and routing are tested at the web level (...ListEverySpecialtyByStoredNameOnOnePage, ...ListEachHolderByFirstThenLastName, ...OpenWhenNoSpecialtyIsRecorded, ...ShowStoredSpecialtyNamesInEveryLanguage).

patterns.description: precedent for a repository over a persisted lookup value referenced by another entity
narrow Repository base with @Transactional(readOnly = true) read methods; SpecialtyRepository mirrors it without @Cacheable
package-private controller, constructor-injected repository, view name under vets/
layout fragment call and full-name rendering as first name, space, last name via th:text
build-time enforcement that every bundle carries every key (REQ-LANG-002)

risks.risk: BaseEntity defines no equals/hashCode, and specialties from SpecialtyRepository are distinct instances from those on the cached vets. Grouping by object equality or contains() silently leaves every specialty with no holders.
risks.mitigation: Match specialties by identity (getId), per system-design § Contracts, Specialty directory invariants. A unit test builds holder specialties as separate instances sharing an id with the listed ones.

risks.risk: Order is not stable if taken from storage: VetRepository.findAll() has no ORDER BY and is cached, and specialty names are indexed but not unique (db/*/schema.sql).
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory imposes a total order itself: specialties by stored name, then identity; holders by last name, then first name, then identity (system-design Specialty directory invariants: order independent of either repository). The stability test permutes input order and asserts identical output; it commits no order beyond that, matching the PRD's stable-only commitment.

risks.risk: Placing inversion, omission, or ordering in the controller adds a fresh business rule to a web controller.
risks.mitigation: architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog Web controller row and Design Validation Checklist: the controller fetches both collections, calls the SpecialtyDirectory factory, adds one model attribute, and returns the view name.

risks.risk: A back-reference from Specialty to its holding vets would change the entity mapping and the serialized /vets route that REQ-VET-001 owns, and could make eager Vet-Specialty-Vet serialization recurse.
risks.mitigation: system-design Specialty directory invariants: Specialty holds no reference to its holders; no entity, mapping, or schema change in this slice (prd-entry non-goal: no change to the veterinarian directory).

risks.risk: SpecialtyDirectory is not framework-instantiated, so the persistence-entity exception does not cover it.
risks.mitigation: architecture-principles § Scoped exception (Does not cover) and § Domain Core: records with List.copyOf defensive copies, no setters; entries hold the stored specialty name and holder first/last names as values, never Vet or Specialty references.

risks.risk: Stored specialty and vet names rendered into HTML.
risks.mitigation: security-principles § Realization, Cross-site scripting row: th:text only, never th:utext; names shown exactly as stored with no message lookup (PRD edge case 6).

risks.risk: Page wording missing from a locale, or a none label under a holderless specialty.
risks.mitigation: Prefer the existing specialties key for the heading. Any new key goes into all eleven bundles under src/main/resources/messages/ (REQ-LANG-002; I18nPropertiesSyncTest). No #{none} label under a holderless specialty (PRD Open Questions: narrowest reading).

risks.risk: Unbounded single-page read of all specialties and all vets.
risks.mitigation: Same whole-roster read the cached findAll() already serves; clinic reference data has no write path (PRD NG-2). Holders come from the cached vet read while specialties are uncached, so an out-of-band edit can surface a specialty before its holders; this is system-design Open Question 5, and no eviction or new cache is added (CacheConfiguration declares only the vet cache).

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; skipped. Verdict minor rather than new: every new type instantiates an in-force catalog pattern inside the existing vet package, and the only durable writes are Contracts rows and one invariants paragraph. No ADR: rejecting a Specialty back-reference is contained in this slice, and a later slice that reopens it records the ADR then. Effort involved: this is the codebase's first non-entity value object and the first hand-written repository doubles in a web test, and the identity-matching pitfall is silent. Pre-existing tension, not widened: Vet references Specialty by object association rather than identity (as Pet does PetType), and the aggregate closed property binds entities too; this slice adds a repository for Specialty on the PetTypeRepository precedent but adds no new reference. Vocabulary: directory is not a ubiquitous-language term, though the PRD already says veterinarian directory; SpecialtyDirectory composes the canonical Specialty with that page term. The product-requirements-expert may choose to add it; this triage writes no vocabulary.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: No request input is bound. SpecialtyController.java:145-146 reads `@GetMapping("/specialties.html")` / `String showSpecialtyDirectory(Model model)`. A grep for `@ModelAttribute|@RequestBody|@RequestParam|@PathVariable` across vet/Specialty*.java found nothing (exit 1), so the mass-assignment, cross-request-state and path-traversal rows of docs/security-principles.md do not apply.

Output escaping is preserved. specialtyList.html renders stored values only through `th:text` (`th:text="${entry.specialtyName()}"`, `th:text="${holder.firstName() + ' ' + holder.lastName()}"`). That matches vetList.html:18 `th:text="${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName}"`. A grep of templates/vets/ for `th:utext` and `__${` found no utext anywhere and no preprocessing in the new template; the only preprocessing hits are the pre-existing, server-computed page numbers in vetList.html:30-50.

Data access is safe from injection. SpecialtyRepository.java:279-280 is a derived `@Transactional(readOnly = true) List<Specialty> findAll()` with no query text. VetRepository.java:44-46 `findAll()` is the existing cached read. Nothing in the change writes data, which is consistent with PRD NG-2.

The exposed surface does not widen beyond the baseline. The new GET route publishes vet names and specialty names that /vets.html and the machine-readable vet route already expose. PRD REQ-VET-003 mandates the unpaged single-page view. Specialties and vets have no write path (NG-2), so an attacker cannot grow the list. It also adds no management endpoint.

Rendered errors cannot leak sensitive data. SpecialtyDirectory only sorts and groups entity fields; it throws no custom exception message. Specialty.name carries `@NotBlank` (NamedEntity.java:34), so the name comparator gets no null from valid seed data.

There are no shell, file, deserialization, logging or secret patterns in the new production code. A grep for `Runtime|ProcessBuilder|exec(|JsonTypeInfo|enableDefaultTyping|Files.|/tmp/|System.out|log.` over vet/Specialty*.java found nothing. The diff adds no credentials, and build.gradle and application properties are not in scripts/changeset.sh --name-only.

Supply chain: the change adds no dependency. build.gradle does not configure OWASP Dependency-Check (a grep for `dependencycheck`/`owasp` found nothing), so no NVD match ran in this review. `./gradlew dependencies` resolves Spring Boot 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, Jackson (tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind) 3.1.5 and Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE.

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: Additive and contained: four new production files in the vet package plus the two doc edits, no existing production code modified. The one new surface is a GET route that binds no input. It reuses the existing cached VetRepository.findAll() without changing it, and the layout menu value matches no nav item, so no other page changes.

semantic_surprise.note: Read SpecialtyDirectory.of end to end. Holders are grouped by specialty id rather than instance equality, which is correct because BaseEntity has no equals. Holderless specialties map to List.of(), vets with no specialty never enter the map, and both comparators are total (specialties by name then id, holders by last name, first name, then id). The template uses th:text only. One residual edge: the name columns are nullable in all three schemas and the comparators are not null-safe, so a null name row would 500 the page. Vet.getSpecialties() already has the same exposure, and the app has no write path.

test_adequacy.note: The tests assert real outcomes. The stable-order test compares a build from reversed inputs against the original, using two same-named specialties with different holders, so dropping the id tie-break would fail it. The vet factory attaches id-only copies of specialties, so instance matching would fail. The controller tests match exact rendered element text in all ten locales. Gaps that do not block: the holder id tie-break is never exercised, the no-specialty-vet omission is tested only below the web layer, and HTML escaping is not pinned.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers in the full-battery roster approved with no findings. But the security approval cites SpecialtyController.java:145-146 and SpecialtyRepository.java:279-280, and those files are 46 and 38 lines long. The numbers are scripts/changeset.sh output offsets, not file lines. The quoted code is accurate, but the citations do not resolve to the files they name. The test-reviewer also left a recommendation that no test pins escaping. The missing OWASP scanner is a standing gap, context rather than a hedge.

scope_deviation.note: The diff matches the design-block primary_paths exactly, and the page is address-only, as the owner deferred navigation. Design revisions 0, consultations 0. The single build retry was the implementer's planned partial checkpoint after cycle 2, not a gate failure.

rationale: The code stays contained, and the hunks read as specified: identity-keyed inversion, total ordering, escaped output. Scrutinize only because two line citations in the security approval point at changeset offsets rather than file lines. Before merging, read the 46-line controller and 27-line template yourself to confirm no input binding and th:text only.
